data.name: YearReview.UnpricedPositions
data.value: {0} position(s) need pricing before this view is fully reliable.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.PositiveCashFlow
data.value: The year shows positive cash-flow capacity: income and contributions covered expenses, which means the financial structure generated room to protect or grow patrimony.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.NegativeCashFlow
data.value: The year closed with pressure on cash flow. Expenses and movements consumed more than the year generated, so the main review point is spending control or income recovery.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.StrongSavings
data.value: The contribution pace is strong compared with annual income. This is usually a healthy sign when liquidity and emergency reserve are not being sacrificed.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.LowSavings
data.value: The contribution pace is still modest compared with annual income. A practical next step is finding one recurring expense or decision that can become monthly investment capacity.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.ConcentratedExpenses
data.value: Expenses are concentrated in one leading category. That category deserves detailed review because a single behavior change there can move the whole year.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.DistributedExpenses
data.value: Expenses are relatively distributed across categories. Improvements will probably come from small recurring adjustments instead of one isolated cut.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.PositiveInvestments
data.value: The current investment position is above applied value. Keep the focus on allocation quality, liquidity needs and whether this return is aligned with the annual plan.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.NegativeInvestments
data.value: The current investment position is below applied value. This does not automatically mean a bad decision, but it asks for review of risk, time horizon and concentration.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.UnpricedPositions
data.value: Some positions still lack reliable pricing. Correcting them will make patrimony, return and annual projection more trustworthy.

data.name: YearReview.Analysis.PricedPositions
data.value: The current position has no pricing gaps flagged by the financial facts service, so the consolidated numbers are in a good state for decision-making.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.CashFlow.Positive.Body
data.value: The year closed with positive capacity after operating expenses and contributions. The priority is preserving this spread and deciding how much becomes reserve, investment and planned spending.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.CashFlow.Negative.Body
data.value: The annual result shows pressure: expenses and movements consumed more than income supported. The first action is separating structural expenses from one-off events before increasing investment commitments.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.ExpenseConcentration.Title
data.value: Expense concentration is the main lever

data.name: YearReview.Insight.ExpenseConcentration.Body
data.value: The largest category is large enough to influence the whole year. Review its recurring items, renegotiate what repeats, and only then look for smaller savings elsewhere.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.ExpenseDistribution.Body
data.value: No single category dominates the year. Improvement probably depends on monthly discipline across several small categories rather than one large isolated cut.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.Savings.Strong.Body
data.value: The contribution rate is strong relative to income. Keep validating whether this pace is compatible with liquidity, emergency reserve and upcoming obligations.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.Savings.Low.Body
data.value: The annual saving rate is not yet strong enough to accelerate patrimony. A practical target is converting one recurring expense or unused cash pocket into monthly contribution capacity.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.Investments.Positive.Body
data.value: The current portfolio is above applied value. The next review is not only return, but whether the best-performing positions are also aligned with risk, concentration and time horizon.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.Investments.Negative.Body
data.value: The current portfolio is below applied value. Check whether the loss is market volatility, missing pricing, currency movement or a concentration problem before changing allocation.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.DataQuality.Warning.Body
data.value: Some positions still need reliable pricing. Fixing them should come before using annual return and patrimony movement as decision-grade indicators.

data.name: YearReview.Insight.DataQuality.Good.Body
data.value: No pricing gap is flagged in the canonical facts. The dashboard can be read as a reliable management view, subject to the normal limits of current-position data.
